methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Drones & Autonomous (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 7 same-sector peers exist in Drones & Autonomous, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Airship Industries is a pre-seed stage company operating in the Drones & Autonomous sector. The available comparable universe consists of eight private companies in the sector, including Waymo, Wayve, Zipline, Joby Aviation, and Nuro. No public peers exist in this narrow space.

Peer-median valuation analysis is not applicable to this engagement. While seven same-sector peers exist, none satisfy the filtering criteria for stage alignment or valuation tier similarity required for meaningful comparison. Specifically, zero pre-seed or adjacent-stage comparables were identified, and zero peers of similar valuation tier were found. The methodology requires a minimum of three datapoints within tightly defined parameters to avoid introducing systematic bias. Relying on the full sector median would conflate vastly different company scales, technologies, and development phases, rendering such an estimate unreliable for a pre-seed investment decision.

Without sufficient narrow-set peer data, traditional triangulation methods do not yield a defensible valuation range. A proper valuation of Airship Industries would require either: direct comparable fundraising milestones from same-stage Drones & Autonomous companies; access to detailed financial or technical metrics distinguishing this company within its sector; or application of venture capital method assumptions tied to specific milestones and exit scenarios. Additional diligence on company-specific fundamentals is necessary before quantifying fair value.
